sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Unit assessment. Work alone, show your steps, and check your work before you finish.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 54°. Find the measure of the corresponding angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 38° and 51°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 102°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 22. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 44, and it is parallel to the third side
11, and it is parallel to the third side
22, and it is parallel to the third side
11, and it is perpendicular to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: Alternate interior angles give two pairs of congruent angles, and the opposite sides are congruent, so the triangles formed are congruent by ASA.
The diagonals are perpendicular, which forces bisection.
Every quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other.
The diagonals are congruent, so they must bisect each other.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 85°. Find the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 73° and 37°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 44°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 94. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 94, and it is parallel to the third side
47, and it is parallel to the third side
188, and it is parallel to the third side
47, and it is perpendicular to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent, after constructing the bisector of the apex angle. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The base angles look equal in the diagram.
The two smaller triangles are congruent by SAS, so their corresponding base angles are congruent.
All triangles have congruent base angles.
The bisector is perpendicular to the base by definition.
